text.p: These are the leading stories in the Turkish press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Seven Turkish ambassadors in Europe have warned Foreign Minister Tansu Ciller against Turkey breaking off its ties with the West.
- Islamist Prime Minister Necmattin Erbakan indexes civil servant salaries to U.S. dollar in the budget for 1997.
- Artist Sanar Yurdatapan detained by police for taking part in pro-Kurdish MED-TV programme.
- Markets caution as Erbakan's order to stop internal borrowing raises worries on whether the state will mint money.
- Turkish Parliament to debate a motion aimed at toppling the new Islamist-led government.
- United Nation report reveals that a third of Turkey is poverty-striken.
- Carmaker TOFAS orders two-day break in production, beginning on Wednesday.
- Eighty percent of drugs in Europe come from Turkey.
- Today's censure motion works to the advantage of the coalition, with expected failure expected to make it stronger.
